typescriptBaseline.limits: Installed dependencies use the candidate lockfile; baseline application sources are retained original bytes.

limits: Separate complete CLI processes; dependency installation and compilation excluded.

A small exec-isolated C meter forks/execs each actual application and calls Linux wait4 for microsecond CPU accounting and child high-water RSS. This excludes Python parent RSS/high-water contamination. Linux CPU includes descendants reaped by the application; ru_maxrss is a maximum, not simultaneous process-tree RSS.

Wall/first-paint timings include the same meter exec/fork/coordination/wait overhead in both arms; meter compilation is excluded. Resource CPU/RSS excludes the meter parent and includes the actual child launch/exec, with a small C-process RSS floor. PTY idle RSS/CPU uses the actual application PID, not the meter.
Fresh isolated HOME per sample; no account, network workload, inference or authenticated performance is measured.

The retained TS package version is supplied through its supported OPENMATES_CLI_LATEST_VERSION override to both backends, suppressing registry update checks in version/startup/TUI; update-check network performance is excluded, not benchmarked.

Signed-out native login and original TypeScript home have different content and input semantics. First-paint/Tab/Escape timings describe their actual screens and must not be presented as equivalent-workload speedups.
Input timing ends at the next synchronized ANSI frame and is not a causal end-to-end interaction guarantee.
Five samples give a coarse p95 (nearest-rank maximum); host scheduling, page cache and language runtime initialization are included.
